negative_findings.description: Direct searches for vendor press releases announcing a signed core-banking contract with a named Montenegrin bank returned nothing specific in either language.
negative_findings.result_summary: English query 'vendor press release contract signed core banking Montenegro bank implementation' returned only generic US core-vendor negotiation content plus the Ripple–CBCG CBDC agreement; Montenegrin query with 'potpisan ugovor' + 'bankarski sistem' returned central-bank/SEPA/instant-payments items, not vendor releases.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's premise in reverse: for a market this small, core-banking wins are largely undisclosed by both sides, so discovery must rely on indirect fingerprints (app package IDs, hosting, job ads, tender bidder lists) rather than press releases.

negative_findings.description: No Diebold Nixdorf or NCR Atleos announcement naming a Montenegrin bank was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query 'Diebold Nixdorf OR "NCR Atleos" Montenegro bank ATM agreement' returned only global vendor-strategy and unrelated-market items (US credit union, PayNearMe, ITCARD).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests the Montenegrin ATM channel runs through regional distributors/integrators (Printec, Asseco/MoneyGet) rather than OEM-direct announcements — so distributor sources should be prioritised over OEM newsrooms.

negative_findings.description: No named digital-onboarding/eKYC vendor was found publicly attached to any Montenegrin bank.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query for Montenegro + 'digital onboarding'/'eKYC' vendor announcements returned only generic vendor marketing (Innovatrics, Microblink, Plaid) and ecosystem overviews.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A live white space: identity/onboarding suppliers to Montenegrin banks are currently unattributed in open sources and will need app-teardown, privacy-policy/processor-list and job-ad techniques.

negative_findings.result_summary: HTTP 403 Forbidden on https://www.printecgroup.com/country/printec-montenegro-en/ despite the page being indexed and summarised in search results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A high-value supplier source for this cell needs a browser-grade collector; recording it as dead on this single failure would lose the single most relevant local vendor.

negative_findings.description: Local-language searching for card personalisation and switch/processing had weak Montenegrin terminology coverage.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries used 'bankomati', 'POS terminali', 'ugovor', 'isporuka', 'saopštenje', 'implementacija', 'potpisan ugovor', 'reference/projekat' — but no validated Montenegrin terms were exercised for card personalisation ('personalizacija kartica'), card switching/processing ('procesiranje kartica', 'kartični switch') or kiosk ('kiosk/uređaji za samouslugu').
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Two of the cell's named solution areas (card personalisation, switch/processing) are therefore under-searched in the local language, so absence of findings for them is not evidence of absence.

coverage_gaps.description: Card personalisation and card switch/processing suppliers to Montenegrin banks were not identified from the supplier side in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run dedicated sr/en queries ('personalizacija kartica', 'procesiranje kartičnih transakcija', 'kartični procesor Crna Gora') and check regional processors (ASEE/Payten, Halcom, Bankart, Multicard, First Data/Fiserv successors) for Montenegro references; inspect bank card T&Cs which often name the processor.

coverage_gaps.description: No per-bank vendor attribution table exists yet for the ~11-15 licensed Montenegrin banks.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a bank-by-bank grid (CKB/OTP, NLB Podgorica, Erste, Hipotekarna, Lovćen, Prva banka, Universal Capital Bank, Addiko, Adriatic Bank, Zapad banka, Ziraat) and populate it from app-store package IDs, web-tech fingerprints, privacy-policy processor lists and job ads before relying on press releases.

coverage_gaps.description: Local vendor primary websites (Logate, ČIKOM, Amplitudo, Printec Montenegro) were identified but their reference/news pages were not directly retrieved, so their customer lists are unread.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch each vendor domain with a browser-grade collector; harvest 'Reference/Klijenti/Projekti/Vijesti' sections and snowball each named institution.

coverage_gaps.description: LinkedIn is repeatedly the richest supplier-announcement channel for this market but is platform-gated and was only sampled indirectly.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Establish a compliant LinkedIn monitoring routine (manual review or licensed tooling) for Printec, ASEE/Payten, Monri, Logate, ČIKOM and Montenegrin bank pages.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor claims are unverified against buyer-side award records (complementary cells 7-8).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Join vendor-announced wins to Montenegrin e-procurement award notices (CJN / ejn.gov.me) and to CRPS company-registry entity data, flagging vendor claims with no corresponding public award as private-bank contracts.

brief: Supplier-side visibility in Montenegro is thin but structurally predictable: global OEMs (NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf) almost never name Montenegrin buyers, while regional distributors and integrators do — Printec Montenegro (transaction automation since 2014), Asseco SEE via its Podgorica-area entity and the MoneyGet ATM network, Halcom in e-banking, and Payten/Monri in POS and e-commerce acquiring. Domestic integrators (Logate, ČIKOM, Amplitudo) publish contract-level detail, including values, in Montenegrin on their own sites, LinkedIn and eKapija, making local-language monitoring mandatory rather than optional. Where no announcement exists at all — which is the norm for core banking and digital onboarding — supplier attribution is still recoverable from unfalsifiable fingerprints such as mobile-app package IDs (e.g. NLB Podgorica's apps carry an Asseco package prefix) and hosting/subdomain evidence. Priority next steps are browser-grade retrieval of the vendor sites (printecgroup.com returned 403), a per-bank vendor attribution grid, and dedicated Montenegrin terminology for card personalisation and switch/processing, which remain unsearched.
